questions.explanation: ω = sqrt(g/L) = sqrt(9.8/0.64) ≈ 3.90 rad/s. Taking the square root undoes the squaring in the underlying relation; squaring instead would give a completely different scale.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Period of a spring oscillator
questions.learningObjective: Compute period from m and k
questions.stem: A mass-spring system is set into oscillation. M=0.5 kg, k=200 N/m. Period?
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k) = 2π√(0.5/200) ≈ 0.314 s. The quotient expresses one given quantity relative to the other; inverting it or adding the two would answer a different question.

questions.topic: Period change when a pendulum is lengthened
questions.stem: Desired pendulum period 2 s. Required length (g=9.8)?
questions.explanation: L = g(T/2π)^2 = 9.8*(2/6.283)^2 ≈ 0.993 m. The quotient expresses one given quantity relative to the other; inverting it or adding the two would answer a different question.

questions.topic: Maximum speed in simple harmonic motion
questions.learningObjective: Compute max speed from energy and omega
questions.stem: SHM energy 0.5 J, m=2 kg, ω=1 rad/s. Maximum speed? (v_max=sqrt(2E/m))
questions.explanation: v_max = sqrt(2E/m) = sqrt(1/2) ≈ 0.707 m/s; also Aω. Taking the square root undoes the squaring in the underlying relation; squaring instead would give a completely different scale.
